result.title: Evidence for contact delocalization in atomic scale friction

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study introduces a two-mass, two-spring model to explain the fine structures in the oscillating motion of atoms during friction force microscopy (FFM). The model demonstrates that the tip can be completely or partially decoupled due to an extremely low effective mass, a finding that is supported by agreement with current high-resolution experiments. The authors use a hybrid computational scheme to simulate the interplay between rapid tip motion and slow cantilever motion, showing that dissipation depends sensitively on surface corrugation.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The text details a two-mass, two-spring model for atomic friction, where the tip apex delocalizes due to ultra-low effective mass and high surface corrugation. It describes the system's dynamics using a Langevin equation for the cantilever and a Monte Carlo algorithm for thermally activated tip apex jumps between potential wells. The model predicts different slip behaviors—from stick-slip to structured and near-dissipationless motion—based on the Tomlinson parameter, which quantifies the number of available potential wells.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The text derives the effective potential and mean surface force for atomic friction, showing that the mean force exhibits discontinuities corresponding to transitions between one-well and two-well tip apex potentials. It confirms that the effective mass of the contact is extremely small, less than $10^{-18}$ kg, based on the observation of intermediate-state slips. The findings suggest that standard interpretations of lateral force amplitude and slip times in FFM measurements may require revision due to the rapid thermal motion of the tip apex.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The text describes two mechanisms for energy dissipation in the tip apex, involving intratip vibrations and apex motion relative to the substrate, both generating phonons. It suggests that these thermally driven dynamics, observed in atomic friction, may be relevant to macroscopic sliding between surfaces. The text also presents figures illustrating slip events and the effect of contact delocalization on tip-surface interaction and mean surface force.
